title: Exceptional localization and costalk transitivity
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and $f:Y\to X$ a compactifiable finite-type morphism of Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use ordinary small etale bounded-below derived categories and $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Write $R\Gamma_x$ for the residue-field-valued supported restriction of [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Exceptional pullback commutes with restriction to an open subscheme and with localization at a point (also with strict localization). More precisely, for $x\in X$ put $X_x=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $Y_x=Y\times_X X_x$, $F=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, and write $f_x:Y_x\to X_x$, $a:F\hookrightarrow Y_x$, and $\pi:F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$a^!f_x^!(M|_{X_x})\cong\pi^!R\Gamma_xM.$$
For any $y\in F$, taking supported restriction at $y$ identifies $R\Gamma_y(f^!M)$ with $R\Gamma_y(\pi^!R\Gamma_xM)$. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, there are natural identifications
$$R\Gamma_z(i^!L)\cong R\Gamma_zL\quad(z\in Z),$$
and for an immediate geometric specialization $z'\rightsquigarrow z$ in $Z$ these identifications carry the normalized residue transition for $i^!L$ to the one for $L$ [def-per-potential-dualizing]. The comparisons commute with compositions of compactifiable morphisms under right-adjoint transitivity and with successive supported restrictions. None of these assertions requires $M$ or $L$ to be potential or putative dualizing.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definition 1.4.1 (closed supported restriction and transitions), Proposition 2.4.3.1 proof (residue-field exceptional transitivity), Lemma 4.4.1 proof (fibrewise reduction); ordinary compact-support localization as in the etale formalism

external.place: Theorem 7.15 and proper base change Theorem 7.16; finite F_ell bounded-below specialization

proof.text: First fix the transitivity comparisons, including their counits. By [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] the ordinary compact-support right adjoints exist, and [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] supplies associative composition isomorphisms on the ambient derived categories. Thus [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] gives $(fg)^!\cong g^!f^!$: its Hom bijection is $\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!Rg_!N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rg_!N,f^!M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,g^!f^!M)$. Its counit is the pasted counit. For a closed immersion $i$, ordinary compact support is $i_*$ (take the compactification $(\mathrm{id},i)$). The supported-kernel adjunction of [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction] is also valid for $\Lambda$-linear maps: its Hom bijection preserves the scalar action because its inclusion and restriction maps do. Since $i_*$ is exact, the support right adjoint preserves injectives by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives]. Applying this Hom bijection to injective resolutions identifies its right derived functor with the compact-support right adjoint, with the same counit. Consequently the $i^!$ in [def-per-potential-dualizing] and the ambient exceptional functor are canonically the same on bounded-below inputs. In particular transitivity for nested closed supports has this normalization.

source.place: XVII, Definition 1.4.1 and Remark 2.4.3.2; support adjunction: Stacks Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic

proof.text:
Open restriction can be proved directly by adjunction. Source restriction $u^*f^!\cong(fu)^!$ is [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], applied to an open immersion $u$. For a cartesian square with open immersions $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ and $u:Y_V\hookrightarrow Y$, put $f_V:Y_V\to V$. For $N\in D(Y_V,\Lambda)$ the same source locality and the ordinary adjunction $v_!\dashv v^*$ give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,u^*f^!M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_!u_!N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(v_!Rf_{V,!}N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,f_V^!v^*M).$$
The middle equality is compact-support composition for $fu=vf_V$, supplied by [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. This proves the claimed open-base comparison by the representing Hom bijections, with their specified counits. All opens are quasi-compact because the schemes are Noetherian; their compactifications are obtained by restricting the open in a compactification of $f$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 4.4.1, locality; ordinary adjunction argument spelled out

proof.text: Work over an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $f^{-1}V$ has a finite affine cover $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite type over $A$. Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_d$. The surjection $A[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\twoheadrightarrow B$, $t_j\mapsto b_j$, of [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] realizes $U\to V$ as $U\xrightarrow{c}P=\mathbf A^d_V\xrightarrow{p}V$, with $c$ closed by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Here the affine description is [def-sbc-affine-space] and $p$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Its standard projective compactification is available by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] and [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Step 1 therefore identifies the exceptional functor of $U\to V$ with $c^!p^!$. This is an explicit polynomial presentation; no factorization theorem requiring a field as base is used.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 4.1.2 after Lemma 4.4.1: closed immersion followed by smooth morphism; polynomial presentation written out

proof.text: For localization at $x\in V$, take $V'=\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak p}$; for strict localization take $V'=X_{(\bar x)}$ with $x\in V$. These are Noetherian: use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] for $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] for the strict-local ring. The map $V'\to V$ is affine ind-etale. In the local case this follows from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations]: $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is the filtered colimit of $A_s$, $s\notin\mathfrak p$; each $A_s=A[t]/(st-1)$ is finitely presented and $\operatorname{Spec}A_s\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. In the strict-local case it is exactly [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale]. Base changing this map to $P$ preserves ind-etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]; it stays affine by the tensor-product presentation. The schemes $P$, $P'=P\times_VV'$, and their closed subschemes $U,U'$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. These check every affine, ind-etale and Noetherian hypothesis needed below.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 2.2.1, localization paragraph; Stacks Tags 00FN and 06LJ for Noetherian permanence

proof.text:
In the base-changed factorization write $c':U'\hookrightarrow P'$, $p':P'\to V'$, and $h:U'\to U$, $q:P'\to P$, $v:V'\to V$. The closed-support comparison [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] and the base-compatible smooth orientation [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation] give the explicit isomorphism
$$h^*c^!p^!M\cong c'^!q^*\bigl(p^*M(d)[2d]\bigr)\cong c'^!\bigl(p'^*v^*M(d)[2d]\bigr)\cong c'^!p'^!v^*M.$$
The twists here are roots-of-unity twists as fixed by the orientation, so the middle equality uses its specified base-change comparison. This proves localization on every affine source chart. To fix the comparison globally, use the natural map $h^*f^!M\to f'^!v^*M$ obtained by adjunction from $Rf'_!h^*f^!M\cong v^*Rf_!f^!M\to v^*M$, using [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. The closed-support comparison is normalized by its counit, and the smooth orientation is base-compatible, so the displayed local isomorphism is this map; the pasting identity [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the comparison for $pc$ with the composite of the two comparisons. Step 2 restricts it to each source chart, hence it is an isomorphism everywhere. Also $c^!$ is the right derived functor of a left exact functor, and $p^!$ is inverse image followed by a fixed shift and twist. The finite affine cover therefore shows $f^!M$ is bounded below whenever $M$ is bounded below. No constructibility or dualizing hypothesis was used.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1 proof and Proposition 2.2.1 localization paragraph; smooth input follows the lecture-notes diagonal/DNC route

proof.text:
Let $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow X_x$ be the closed-point inclusion. The equality of morphisms $f_xa=i_x\pi$, followed by the normalized transitivity of Step 1, gives
$$a^!f_x^!(M|_{X_x})\cong(f_xa)^!(M|_{X_x})\cong(i_x\pi)^!(M|_{X_x})\cong\pi^!i_x^!(M|_{X_x})=\pi^!R\Gamma_xM.$$
The last equality is the residue-field-valued definition of $R\Gamma_x$ in [def-per-potential-dualizing]. All these are compactifiable finite-type maps over the Noetherian local base or its residue field; the closed immersion $a$ is the base change of the closed point, and $\pi$ has the base-changed compactification of $f$. The Hom bijections of [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] and the compact-support composition comparison [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] make this isomorphism natural in $M$.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.1 proof and Lemma 4.4.1 fibrewise reduction

proof.text:
For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and $z\in Z$, set $T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,z}$, $W=Z\times_YT=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, and let $t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow W$, $s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow T$. Localization for the closed immersion: first restrict to an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ containing $z$, by Step 2 applied to $i$ (its restriction over $V$ is the closed immersion $i^{-1}V\hookrightarrow V$, and $\mathcal O_{V,z}=\mathcal O_{Y,z}$, $\mathcal O_{i^{-1}V,z}=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$). Then $T\to V$ is affine ind-etale and $T$ is Noetherian by Step 4, so [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] applies to $T\to V$; no affineness of $T\to Y$ for nonseparated $Y$ is used. Thus
$$R\Gamma_z(i^!L)=t^!((i^!L)|_W)\cong t^!i_T^!(L|_T)\cong(i_Tt)^!(L|_T)=s^!(L|_T)=R\Gamma_zL.$$
The local rings and residue field here are the quotient local ring and the same residue field, by the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The middle comparison is exactly the normalized right-adjoint transitivity of Step 1, not merely an equality of supports. This proves the closed-immersion costalk assertion over the residue-field etale site, before taking geometric fibres.

source.place: XVII, Definition 1.4.1, the vertical costalk identifications, expanded using local closed immersions

proof.text:
For $y\in F$, put $x=f(y)$. The local ring of $Y_x$ at $y$ is $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$: every base element outside the prime of $x$ is already a unit in $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. The residue fields also agree. Hence [def-per-potential-dualizing] identifies the costalk at $y$ of an object restricted from $Y$ to $Y_x$ with its original costalk. Step 5 therefore gives $R\Gamma_y(f^!M)\cong R\Gamma_y(f_x^!(M|_{X_x}))$. Apply the closed-immersion costalk comparison of Step 7 to $a:F\hookrightarrow Y_x$, and then apply $R\Gamma_y$ to Step 6. Their composite is
$$R\Gamma_y(f^!M)\cong R\Gamma_y(a^!f_x^!(M|_{X_x}))\cong R\Gamma_y(\pi^!R\Gamma_xM),$$
which is precisely the pointwise fibre comparison in the statement.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, fibrewise reduction, with the local-ring identification written out

proof.text:
It remains to check the transition maps for $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$. Take an immediate geometric specialization $\bar z'\rightsquigarrow\bar z$ in $Z$. After strict localization at $\bar z$, its reduced one-dimensional closure $C$ is the same closed reduced subscheme whether formed in $Z_{(\bar z)}$ or in $Y_{(\bar z)}$. Write $c:C\hookrightarrow Z_{(\bar z)}$ and $i_{(\bar z)}:Z_{(\bar z)}\hookrightarrow Y_{(\bar z)}$. The identification $Z_{(\bar z)}=Z\times_YY_{(\bar z)}$ is precisely [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian]; [lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction] supplies the strict-local interpretation of the costalks. As in Step 7, first restrict to an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ containing the image of $\bar z$ (Step 2); $Y_{(\bar z)}=V_{(\bar z)}\to V$ is affine ind-etale with Noetherian source by Step 4. The closed-support exchange [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] for this map and Step 1 identify the two complexes on $C$ by
$$c^!\bigl((i^!L)|_{Z_{(\bar z)}}\bigr)\cong c^!i_{(\bar z)}^!(L|_{Y_{(\bar z)}})\cong(i_{(\bar z)}c)^!(L|_{Y_{(\bar z)}}).$$
In the definition [def-per-potential-dualizing], both transitions are therefore formed from this same complex on $C$, the same normalization $\nu:\widetilde C\to C$, and the same degree $[\kappa(\widetilde z_0):\kappa(z_0)]$ after strict localization. The naturality of the trait transition in [lem-per-trait-residue-model] carries this isomorphism to equality of the two normalized transitions, with identical twists and shifts. The endpoint identifications are those of Step 7 by associativity of the closed-support adjunctions. Thus this checks the transition itself, rather than just its source and target.

source.place: XVII, Definition 1.4.1, using Definitions 1.2.3.1 and 1.3.1 for the normalized trait transition

proof.text: Finally, all transitivity comparisons were defined by the Hom bijections with pasted counits in Step 1. Their associativity follows from the associative compact-support comparisons [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] and the normalized composite adjunction [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. The comparison maps of Step 5 are the counit mates of those compact-support exchanges; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] makes their horizontal and vertical pastings equal to the mate for the pasted square. The isomorphisms in Steps 6--8 are composites of exactly these transitivity and localization maps. Thus replacing $f$ by a composite or taking two successive closed supported restrictions yields the same comparisons. In Step 9 the common-complex description also respects these maps by naturality of [lem-per-trait-residue-model]. This proves the asserted composition and supported-restriction compatibilities for arbitrary bounded-below $M,L$.
